senses.title: A spiral form
senses.definition: a shape that winds around like a screw thread
senses.definitionCN: 像螺纹一样盘绕的形状
senses.example: The staircase winds in a screw.
senses.exampleCN: 楼梯呈螺旋形盘旋。
senses.why: The shape that lets a screw grip becomes a general form.
senses.whyCN: 让螺丝咬合的形态成为一种普遍形状。

senses.title: To ruin or cheat
senses.definition: to ruin something, or to cheat someone, in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中搞砸某事或欺骗某人
senses.example: He screwed the deal by arriving late.
senses.exampleCN: 他因迟到把交易搞砸了。
senses.why: A twisted thread becomes an image of things going wrong.
senses.whyCN: 扭曲的螺纹成为事情出错的意象。

intro.en: Screw probably comes from Old French escroue, a nut or screw, perhaps from Latin scrofa, a sow.
intro.cn: screw 可能源自古法语 escroue（螺母、螺丝），也许来自拉丁语 scrofa（母猪）。

items.en: Scrofa meant a sow, perhaps because of the curled shape.
items.cn: scrofa 意为母猪，可能因卷曲形状而得名。

items.en: Escroue meant a nut or a screw.
items.cn: escroue 意为螺母或螺丝。

items.en: Screw named a spiral fastening device.
items.cn: screw 指螺旋紧固装置。

items.en: Screw also meant to turn something into place.
items.cn: screw 也开始表示旋转固定。

items.en: Screw has informal senses of ruining or cheating.
items.cn: 现代英语中 screw 有搞砸或欺骗的非正式义。

note.en: Screw is compared with similar-looking words and with words for fasteners and turning.
note.cn: 把 screw 与形近词以及表示紧固件和旋转的词作比较。

entries.definition: a metal pin used to fasten
to move something in a circle

normalIntro.en: A screw is a spiral fastener, and to screw is to turn it.
normalIntro.cn: screw 是螺旋紧固件，to screw 就是旋转它。

normal.en: A screwdriver turns a screw.
normal.cn: 螺丝刀转动螺丝。

normal.en: Screw the lid on tightly.
normal.cn: 把盖子拧紧。

normal.en: Unscrew means turn the other way.
normal.cn: unscrew 意为反方向拧开。

normal.en: Screw up means ruin something.
normal.cn: screw up 意为搞砸。

normal.en: A loose screw makes a chair wobble.
normal.cn: 松动的螺丝让椅子摇晃。

abstract.en: A spiral turns forward motion into grip.
abstract.cn: 螺旋把前进运动变成抓合力。

abstract.en: The same turning motion can fix or destroy.
abstract.cn: 同样的旋转动作既能固定，也能破坏。

abstract.en: The tool and its shape share one short word.
abstract.cn: 工具与它的形状共用一个短词。

examples.en: Tighten the screw with a screwdriver.
examples.cn: 用螺丝刀把螺丝拧紧。

examples.en: He screwed the lid onto the jar.
examples.cn: 他把盖子拧到罐子上。

examples.en: She screwed up the plan.
examples.cn: 她把计划搞砸了。

dict_mnemonic.text: screw 可能经古法语 escroue 来自拉丁语 scrofa（母猪），因螺旋形似猪尾而得名；核心是「螺旋纹的紧固件」。

root: 可能经古法语 escroue 源自拉丁语 scrofa（母猪），核心义「带螺旋纹、可旋转固定的物件」。

sensesIntro.en: Screw means a spiral fastener, to turn it, a spiral form, or to ruin something informally.
sensesIntro.cn: screw 意为螺丝、拧紧、螺旋，或非正式地搞砸。

core.en: A spiral that grips as it turns.
core.cn: 旋转时产生咬合的螺旋。

branches.en: The metal fastener itself.
branches.cn: 金属紧固件本身。

branches.en: The act of turning it into place.
branches.cn: 把它旋转固定到位的动作。

branches.en: The spiral shape of the thread.
branches.cn: 螺纹的螺旋形状。

branches.en: A plan twisted into failure.
branches.cn: 被扭曲至失败的计划。

branches.en: The object and its use are inseparable.
branches.cn: 物件与用途不可分割。

intro.en: Screw forms tools, adjectives, and common phrasal verbs.
intro.cn: screw 构成工具、形容词与常用短语动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin scrofa is a possible distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scrofa 是可能的远源。

items.meaning: a fastener, or to turn it

items.example: The box of screws is open.
The lid is screwed on tight.
He is screwing the shelf to the wall.
items.exampleCN: 他正在把架子拧到墙上。

items.meaning: to ruin or make a mistake
items.example: Do not screw up the interview.

definition_en: the written text of a film or play, a system of writing, a person's handwriting, or a set of computer instructions
core_image: 桌上摊开一份剧本，页边写满演员用铅笔做的批注
scene: 演员们在开拍前围读剧本。The actors read the script together before filming.
sceneCN: 这里 script 是「剧本」（第 1 个义项）；句意：演员们在开拍前围读剧本。

senses.title: A text for a film or play
senses.definition: the written words and directions for a film, play, or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 电影、戏剧或广播的台词与说明文字
senses.example: The script needs another rewrite.
senses.exampleCN: 这个剧本还需要再改一稿。
senses.why: The central modern sense is the text actors follow.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是演员照读的文本。

senses.title: A system of writing
senses.definition: a set of written symbols used by a language
senses.definitionCN: 某种语言使用的一套书写符号
senses.example: These languages use different scripts.
senses.exampleCN: 这些语言使用不同的文字体系。
senses.why: Any written text is a script, so a whole writing system took the name.
senses.whyCN: 任何写下的文本都是 script，于是整套书写系统也用了这个词。

senses.title: A person's handwriting
senses.definition: the way a particular person writes by hand
senses.definitionCN: 某个人手写时的字体样式
senses.example: His script is small and neat.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笔迹小而工整。
senses.why: Handwriting is the most personal kind of written text.
senses.whyCN: 笔迹是最个人化的书写文本。

senses.title: Computer instructions
senses.definition: a set of instructions that a computer follows
senses.definitionCN: 计算机按顺序执行的一组指令
senses.example: The script runs every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个脚本每天早上运行。
senses.why: A script is a text a machine reads and follows.
senses.whyCN: 脚本是机器阅读并执行的文本。

intro.en: Script comes from Latin scriptum, something written, from scribere, to write.
intro.cn: script 源自拉丁语 scriptum（写下的东西），来自 scribere（写）。

items.en: Scribere meant to write.
items.cn: scribere 意为写。

items.en: Scriptum meant something written.
items.cn: scriptum 意为写下的东西。

items.en: Script meant a written document.
items.cn: script 意为书面文件。

items.en: Script came to mean the text of a play.
items.cn: script 开始指戏剧文本。

items.en: Script also names writing systems and computer code.
items.cn: 现代英语中 script 还指书写体系与计算机代码。

note.en: Script is compared with similar-looking words and with words for written texts.
note.cn: 把 script 与形近词以及表示书面文本的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Script is anything written, from a play to computer code.
normalIntro.cn: script 是任何写下来的东西，从剧本到计算机代码。

normal.en: Actors read a script.
normal.cn: 演员读剧本。

normal.en: Different languages use different scripts.
normal.cn: 不同语言使用不同文字体系。

normal.en: Neat script means neat handwriting.
normal.cn: neat script 意为工整的笔迹。

normal.en: A computer script runs instructions.
normal.cn: 计算机脚本执行指令。

normal.en: A scriptwriter writes scripts.
normal.cn: scriptwriter 写剧本。

abstract.en: Writing turns speech into something that can be followed.
abstract.cn: 书写把言语变成可以照做的事。

abstract.en: A play, a writing system, and code are all texts to be read.
abstract.cn: 戏剧、文字体系与代码都是供阅读的文本。

abstract.en: Script links human writing with machine reading.
abstract.cn: script 把人类书写与机器读取连接起来。

examples.en: The script needs another rewrite.
examples.cn: 这个剧本还需要再改一稿。

examples.en: These languages use different scripts.
examples.cn: 这些语言使用不同的文字体系。

examples.en: The script runs every morning.
examples.cn: 这个脚本每天早上运行。

dict_mnemonic.text: script 源自拉丁语 scribere（写），script 就是「写下来的东西」，所以既指文字、笔迹，也指剧本和脚本。

root: 源自拉丁语 scriptum（写下的东西），来自 scribere（写），核心义「书写下来的文本」。

sensesIntro.en: Script means a film or play text, a writing system, handwriting, or computer instructions.
sensesIntro.cn: script 意为影视剧本、文字体系、笔迹，或计算机脚本。

core.en: A written text that others follow.
core.cn: 供他人照读或执行的书写文本。

branches.en: The text actors perform.
branches.cn: 演员表演所用的文本。

branches.en: The symbols a language writes with.
branches.cn: 一种语言书写所用的符号。

branches.en: A person's own hand.
branches.cn: 个人的手写字体。

branches.en: Instructions a machine reads.
branches.cn: 机器读取的指令。

branches.en: Both are texts meant to be read.
branches.cn: 两者都是供阅读的文本。

intro.en: Script forms words for writers, documents, and notes.
intro.cn: script 构成表示作者、文件与附言的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin scribere and scriptum are the sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scribere 与 scriptum 是词源。

items.example: The desk is covered with scripts.

items.exampleCN: 这个节目感觉太照本宣科了。
编写脚本能节省数小时工作。

items.example: The manuscript is in the archive.

items.meaning: a note added after a letter
a character set below the line

definition_en: a three-dimensional work of art made by shaping or carving material; the art of making such works
core_image: 工作室中央立着一块尚未完成的大理石人像，肩上落满石粉，四周是锤子和凿子
scene: 美术馆把一座青铜人像安放在中庭，观众可以绕着它走一圈。The gallery placed a bronze sculpture in the courtyard so visitors could walk around it.
sceneCN: 这里 sculpture 指「雕塑作品」（第 1 个义项：三维立体造型艺术品）；句意为美术馆把一件青铜雕塑放在中庭，让观众可以绕行观看。图中可辨识物件：青铜人像、基座、天窗、参观者。

pos.zh: 雕塑；雕刻成形（较少用，常用「雕刻」这一动词形式）

derivatives.zh: 雕塑；造型（由名词截短而来）
雕刻成的；有立体造型的

senses.title: A three-dimensional work of art
senses.definition: a work of art made by shaping, carving or casting material in three dimensions
senses.definitionCN: 通过塑形、雕刻或铸造材料而成的三维艺术品
senses.example: The bronze sculpture dominates the entrance hall.
senses.exampleCN: 那件青铜雕塑占据了入口大厅。
senses.why: sculpture comes from Latin sculptura 'a carving', so the object and the act were one word from the start.
senses.whyCN: sculpture 来自拉丁 sculptura「雕刻物」，因此物件与动作从一开始就共用一个词。

senses.title: The art of making such works
senses.definition: the art or practice of making three-dimensional forms
senses.definitionCN: 制作三维造型的艺术或实践
senses.example: He turned from painting to sculpture at thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 他三十岁时从绘画转向雕塑。
senses.why: the uncountable use names the discipline, just as painting names an art rather than one canvas.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法命名这门学科，正如「绘画」命名一门艺术而非一幅画。

senses.title: A single carved or cast figure
senses.definition: one figure or object carved, modelled or cast from stone, metal or wood
senses.definitionCN: 用石、金属或木料雕成、塑成或铸成的一件形象或器物
senses.example: A marble sculpture of a hand rests on the plinth.
senses.exampleCN: 一只大理石手部雕塑放在基座上。
senses.why: the countable use treats the art object as one item among many in a collection.
senses.whyCN: 可数用法把这件艺术品当作收藏中的一件。

senses.title: To shape material into a figure
senses.definition: to shape or carve material into a three-dimensional form
senses.definitionCN: 把材料雕琢或塑造成三维形体
senses.example: The artist sculptured the figure from a single block.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术家用一整块石料雕出这个人物。
senses.why: the verb is simply the noun put to work, and modern English often prefers the shorter sculpt.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词直接用作动作，现代英语更常用更短的动词形式。

senses.title: A natural form that looks carved
senses.titleCN: 天然形成的雕塑状地貌
senses.definition: a rock or landform whose shape seems deliberately modelled
senses.definitionCN: 形状仿佛经刻意塑形的岩石或地貌
senses.example: Wind and salt have made a sculpture of the coastal rock.
senses.exampleCN: 风与盐把海岸岩石雕成了一件作品。
senses.why: the word extends to nature whenever erosion produces something that looks made by a sculptor.
senses.whyCN: 当侵蚀造出仿佛雕塑家所做的形状时，这个词就扩展到自然。

senses.title: Raised carving on a flat surface
senses.definition: carving in which figures are raised from a flat background, as on a frieze
senses.definitionCN: 形象从平面背景凸出的雕刻，如横饰带上的浮雕
senses.example: A relief sculpture of dancers runs along the frieze.
senses.exampleCN: 一条横饰带上有一列舞者的浮雕。
senses.why: relief is sculpture still attached to its block, and English names it by adding the qualifier relief.
senses.whyCN: 浮雕仍是连着石块的雕塑，英语加「浮雕」这一限定词来命名。

senses.title: A public monument
senses.definition: a large outdoor work, often commemorative, placed in a public space
senses.definitionCN: 置于公共空间的大型户外作品，常具纪念性
senses.example: The city unveiled a sculpture honouring the dock workers.
senses.exampleCN: 该市为纪念码头工人揭幕了一座雕塑。
senses.why: public art made sculpture a civic object, so the word now also names monuments by its own name.
senses.whyCN: 公共艺术使雕塑成为城市物件，于是这个词也直接用来指纪念碑。

senses.title: An ephemeral work such as ice sculpture
senses.definition: a temporary work made of melting or fragile material, created for an event
senses.definitionCN: 为活动而作、用易融或易碎材料制成的临时作品
senses.example: The ice sculpture melted before the speeches ended.
senses.exampleCN: 冰雕在致辞结束前就融化了。
senses.why: because the definition depends on three-dimensional shaping rather than permanence, ice and sand qualify.
senses.whyCN: 因为定义取决于三维塑形而非永久性，冰与沙也符合条件。

intro.en: Sculpture comes from Latin sculptura 'a carving', from sculpere 'to carve, cut out'. English took it through French and Italian forms in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sculpture 来自拉丁 sculptura「雕刻物」，源自动词 sculpere「雕刻、削出」。英语在十六世纪经法语与意大利语形式借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sculpere meant 'to carve, cut out, shape by cutting'. It is generally connected with the idea of cutting, and related forms appear in scalprum 'a chisel'.
items.cn: sculpere 意为「雕刻、削出、以切削成形」。一般认为它与「切」这一概念相关，相关形态见于 scalprum「凿子」。

items.en: The noun sculptura named both the act of carving and the carved object, a double sense English inherited.
items.cn: 名词 sculptura 兼指雕刻动作与雕刻成品，英语继承了这个双重含义。

items.en: Renaissance Italian scultura and French sculpture carried the word into English, where it settled in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的意大利语 scultura 与法语 sculpture 把这个词带入英语，十六世纪定型。

items.en: Stone, bronze, wood and clay were all covered, with casting treated as sculpture as much as carving.
items.cn: 石、青铜、木与黏土都包括在内，铸造与雕刻同样被视为雕塑。

items.en: Public monuments and modern temporary works widened the word beyond gallery pieces.
items.cn: 公共纪念碑与现代临时作品把这个词扩展到画廊作品之外。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin base of sculpere is reconstructed, and its exact relation to scalprum and to the cutting family is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：sculpere 的拉丁语前词基属于重构形式，它与 scalprum 及「切」词族的确切关系仍有争论。

note.en: Group one holds the word's own family and one scalpel look-alike from the same cutting stock; group two holds kinds of three-dimensional work that are not synonyms of sculpture.
note.cn: 第一组是这个词自身的词族，外加一个同出「切」词族的形近词；第二组是并非 sculpture 同义词的三维作品类别。

entries.definition: The artist who makes sculpture, formed with the agent ending -or; it names a person, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 制作雕塑的艺术家，用施事后缀 -or 构成；指人，不指作品。

entries.definition: The clipped modern verb meaning to make a sculpture, more common than sculpture as a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 截短而来的现代动词，意为制作雕塑，作动词时比 sculpture 更常用。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of sculpture' or 'like sculpture'; it describes a quality, not an object.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「雕塑的」或「像雕塑的」形容词；描述性质，不指物件。

entries.definition: A small surgical knife, from Latin scalprum 'chisel'; it shares the cutting idea with sculpture but is not the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 外科小刀，来自拉丁 scalprum「凿子」；与 sculptura 共享「切」的概念，但并非同一个词。

entries.definition: A carved or cast figure of a person or animal, usually life-size or larger; it is one kind of sculpture.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物的雕铸形象，通常与真人等大或更大；是雕塑的一种。

entries.definition: An object or design cut into wood or stone; it stresses the cutting process and often decoration rather than free-standing art.
entries.definitionCN: 在木石上刻出的物件或纹样；强调切削过程，常指装饰而非独立艺术品。

entries.definition: Carving whose figures stand out from a flat background; it is sculpture still attached to its block.
entries.definitionCN: 形象从平面背景凸出的雕刻；仍是连着石块的雕塑。

entries.definition: A sculpture of a person's head and shoulders, a subtype defined by what it shows.
entries.definitionCN: 人像头部与肩部的雕塑，按所表现的范围界定的一种类型。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real museum phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实博物馆短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin sculpere 'carve' plus -ura gives sculpture: the carved thing and the carving act.
normal.cn: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻」加 -ura 构成 sculpture：既是刻成之物，也是雕刻动作。

normal.en: The family runs sculpt, sculptor, sculpture, sculptural, sculptured.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sculpt、sculptor、sculpture、sculptural、sculptured。

normal.en: Museum labels mark the types: bronze sculpture, marble sculpture, relief sculpture.
normal.cn: 博物馆标签标出类型：青铜雕塑、大理石雕塑、浮雕。

normal.en: Relief sculpture is still attached to its background; free-standing sculpture is not.
normal.cn: 浮雕仍连着背景；独立雕塑则否。

normal.en: Ice sculpture shows that the word needs shaping, not permanence.
normal.cn: 冰雕说明这个词需要的是塑形，而非永久。

abstract.en: Picture a block of stone that has one figure hidden inside it and one way to get it out.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头里藏着一个形象，只有一条路能把它取出来。

abstract.en: Picture a person walking around a figure and seeing a different work from every side.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人绕着雕像走，每换一面就看到一件不同的作品。

abstract.en: Picture a shape that exists only for one afternoon before the sun takes it back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个形状只存在一个下午，随后被太阳收回。

examples.en: The sculpture weighs more than a small car.
examples.cn: 这件雕塑比一辆小汽车还重。

examples.en: She teaches sculpture at the art school.
examples.cn: 她在艺术学校教雕塑。

examples.en: The park holds a sculpture made of weathered steel.
examples.cn: 公园里有一件用耐候钢制成的雕塑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sculpt（雕刻）+ ure」——刻出来的东西 → 雕塑

root: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻、削出」→ sculptura「雕刻物、雕刻」→ 经意大利语与法语进入英语 sculpture。sculpere 的拉丁语前词基为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from one carved object to the art itself, then to natural rock, relief, public monuments and ice that melts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一件刻成的物件走向艺术本身，再走向天然岩石、浮雕、公共纪念碑与会融化的冰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure released from a block by cutting away everything that is not the figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：把不是形象的部分全部削去，让形象从石块中脱出。

branches.en: OBJECT: one three-dimensional work and one carved figure are the countable core of the word.
branches.cn: 物件：一件三维作品与一件雕成形象，是这个词可数的核心。

branches.en: ART AND ACT: the discipline and the verb both name the shaping of material.
branches.cn: 艺术与动作：学科与动词都命名对材料的塑形。

branches.en: NATURE: erosion can produce what looks like deliberate carving.
branches.cn: 自然：侵蚀能造出仿佛刻意雕出的形状。

branches.en: ATTACHED AND PUBLIC: relief stays on its wall, while monuments stand free in civic space.
branches.cn: 附着与公共：浮雕留在墙上，纪念碑则独立于城市空间。

branches.en: TEMPORARY: ice shows that shaping, not lasting, defines the word.
branches.cn: 临时：冰雕说明定义这个词的是塑形，而非长久。

intro.en: Sculpture is a Latin verb plus a Latin result suffix, with an English agent noun and adjective built on the same stem.
intro.cn: sculpture 是拉丁动词加拉丁结果后缀，同一词干上还构成英语施事名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sculpere 'carve' gives sculptura, sculptor and sculptilis; the same cutting idea appears in scalprum 'chisel'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sculpere「雕刻」衍生 sculptura、sculptor 与 sculptilis；同样的「切」意也见于 scalprum「凿子」。

items.example: The root carries the act of cutting away.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「削去」的动作。

items.meaning: the result or act of an action
items.meaningCN: 动作的结果或动作本身
items.example: The suffix forms the noun of result.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成结果名词。

items.meaning: a carving; the art of carving
items.example: The Latin noun already held both senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已兼含两义。

items.meaning: three-dimensional art or a work of it
items.example: The sculpture is cast in bronze.
The sculptor worked only at night.
items.exampleCN: 这位雕塑家只在夜里工作。

items.structure: sculpture clipped to a verb stem
items.example: She sculpts in clay and plaster.
items.exampleCN: 她用黏土和石膏做雕塑。

items.example: The fabric has a sculptural fold.
items.exampleCN: 这块布料有雕塑般的褶。

items.meaningCN: 雕刻成的；具雕塑造型的
items.exampleCN: 花园里有修剪成雕塑形的树篱。

items.example: Relief sculpture covers the temple wall.

definition_zh: 海床；海底（尤指作为水下土地与底土上表面的那一层）
definition_en: the bottom of the sea, especially considered as the underwater land and the surface that lies under shallow or coastal water
core_image: 把海水抽干后露出的那层湿沙与岩石，边界像一块被水盖住的地籍图
scene: 退潮后的浅湾露出湿沙，渔民拖着网在浅水里走。 Anchors had scarred the seabed near the old pier.
sceneCN: 这里 seabed 指「浅海或近岸的水下底部」（第 1 个义项：近岸海底的沙泥表面）；句意为旧码头附近的锚痕划伤了海床。图中可辨识物件：湿沙、渔网、旧木桩、浅水。

senses.title: Bottom of shallow or coastal sea
senses.definition: the bottom of the sea, especially in coastal waters where it can be reached or worked
senses.definitionCN: 海洋的底部，尤指可以到达或施工的近岸水域底部
senses.example: Anchors had scarred the seabed near the old pier.
senses.exampleCN: 旧码头附近的锚痕划伤了海床。
senses.why: seabed is sea plus bed: a bed is the surface one lies on, so the word pictures the sea as a place with a place to rest.
senses.whyCN: seabed 是 sea 加 bed：床是躺卧其上的表面，因此这个词把海想象成一个有处可躺的地方。

senses.title: Underwater land
senses.titleCN: 水下的土地（法律与管辖意义）
senses.definition: the sea bottom treated as land that can be owned, leased or regulated
senses.definitionCN: 把海底当作可拥有、出租或受管辖的土地
senses.example: The Crown holds title to the seabed within territorial waters.
senses.exampleCN: 王室拥有领海内海床的所有权。
senses.why: property law needs a surface to attach rights to, and the seabed supplies that underwater ground.
senses.whyCN: 财产法需要一张可附着权利的表面，海底正好提供这块水下地面。

senses.title: Sediment skin of the sea bottom
senses.definition: the layer of sand, mud and gravel that forms the actual surface of the bottom
senses.definitionCN: 构成底部实际表面的沙、泥与砾石层
senses.example: A thin layer of sand covers the bedrock seabed here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里一层薄沙覆盖在基岩海床上。
senses.why: the bed you touch is the sediment, so the word often means that skin rather than the rock beneath.
senses.whyCN: 能触摸到的床面是沉积物，因此这个词常指这层表皮，而非下面的岩石。

senses.title: Base for underwater structures
senses.definition: the bottom considered as the ground on which cables, pipelines or foundations rest
senses.definitionCN: 作为电缆、管道或基础依托之处的底部
senses.example: Engineers mapped the seabed along the cable route.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测绘了电缆路线沿线的海床。
senses.why: builders need a firm bed under water, and the compound's literal image fits that need exactly.
senses.whyCN: 施工者需要水下一块坚实的床面，这个复合词的字面意象正好对应这一需要。

senses.title: Benthic habitat
senses.definition: the bottom as the living place of organisms that attach to or crawl over it
senses.definitionCN: 作为附着或爬行其上的生物生活场所的底部
senses.example: Oyster reefs once covered much of the estuary seabed.
senses.exampleCN: 牡蛎礁曾覆盖这片河口海床的大部分。
senses.why: animals that live on the bed turn it into a habitat, so seabed can name a living community's ground.
senses.whyCN: 生活在床面上的动物把海床变成栖息地，因此 seabed 可指一个生物群落的基底。

senses.title: Site of mineral extraction
senses.definition: the bottom as a source of sand, gravel, nodules or other minerals
senses.definitionCN: 作为沙、砾石、结核或其他矿产来源的底部
senses.example: The company applied for a licence to mine the seabed.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司申请了海床采矿许可。
senses.why: when the bottom is dug for materials, the word shifts from surface to resource site.
senses.whyCN: 当底部被挖取材料时，这个词就从表面义转向资源场所义。

senses.title: Bottom terrain
senses.definition: the shape of the underwater bottom, including banks, channels and scour marks
senses.definitionCN: 水下底部的形状，包括沙洲、水道与冲刷痕
senses.example: Tidal currents carve ridges across the sandy seabed.
senses.exampleCN: 潮流在沙质海床上刻出一道道脊。
senses.why: the bed has its own relief, just as a field does, so the word also names bottom terrain.
senses.whyCN: 海床有自己的起伏，正如田野有起伏，因此这个词也指底部地形。

senses.title: Boundary between water and subsoil
senses.definition: the dividing surface between the water column above and the solid subsoil below
senses.definitionCN: 上方水柱与下方固体底土之间的分界面
senses.example: Samples were taken right at the seabed to compare pore water.
senses.exampleCN: 样品正好取在海床处，以比较孔隙水。
senses.why: science needs a line where water ends and soil begins, and the seabed is that line.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一条水结束、土开始的界线，而海床正是这条线。

intro.en: Seabed is a native English compound of sea, from Old English sǣ, and bed, from Old English bedd 'bed, couch'. The compound is recorded from the early modern period. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: seabed 是英语本族复合词，由古英语 sǣ「海」与古英语 bedd「床、卧榻」构成。这个复合词在近代早期已有书证。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sǣ meant 'sea, lake, sheet of water' and belongs to the Germanic stock of English. Its earlier origin is not settled.
items.cn: sǣ 意为「海、湖、一片水域」，属于英语的日耳曼语词库。它更早的来源没有定论。

items.en: Bedd meant 'bed, couch, resting place', and was soon used for the bottom of a river or sea.
items.cn: bedd 意为「床、卧榻、休憩之处」，很快也用于河或海的底部。

items.en: The compound sea bed was formed by analogy with riverbed, treating the sea as a body with a bed of its own.
items.cn: sea bed 这个复合词依 riverbed 的类推构成，把海看作一个有自己的床的水体。

items.en: Modern law and offshore industry made seabed a familiar term for underwater land and its resources.
items.cn: 现代法律与近海工业使 seabed 成为指水下土地及其资源的常用词。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Germanic roots of sea and bed are reconstructed, and the exact first citation of the compound is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：sea 与 bed 在日耳曼语之前的词根均为重构形式，复合词的最早书证年代也未固定。

note.en: Group one holds the competing and related names for the sea bottom; group two holds general words that can mean a bottom only in context.
note.cn: 第一组是海洋底部的并用名称与相关名称；第二组是只有在语境中才能指底部的通用词。

entries.definition: A near synonym used especially in geology and oceanography; seabed is more common in law, industry and general British prose.
entries.definitionCN: 近义词，尤用于地质学与海洋学；seabed 更常见于法律、工业与英式一般文字。

entries.definition: The two-word spelling of the same compound, not a different feature; house style decides which form appears.
entries.definitionCN: 同一复合词的分写形式，并非另一种事物；用哪种形式取决于体例。

entries.definition: The industry of extracting minerals from the bottom; it contains seabed but names an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 从海底提取矿产的行业；它虽含 seabed，却指一种活动。

entries.definition: The bottom of a river, built on the same bed pattern; it is the model that seabed follows, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 河底，按同一 bed 模式构成；它是 seabed 仿照的模型，并非同义词。

entries.definition: The lowest part of anything; context is needed before it means the sea bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物的最低部分；需要上下文才指海底。

entries.definition: The bottom of a watercourse or sea; it is the simple noun from which seabed is built.
entries.definitionCN: 水道或海的底部；它是构成 seabed 的简单名词。

entries.definition: The solid surface beneath water or feet; it stresses what can bear weight rather than the marine setting.
entries.definitionCN: 水下或脚下的坚实表面；强调承重，而非海洋环境。

entries.definition: The bottom surface of a space, used figuratively for the sea in seafloor; it shares the image but not the spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 空间的地面，在 seafloor 中借喻海底；共享意象但拼写不同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sea + bed: the sea given a bed to rest on.
normal.cn: sea「海」+ bed「床」：给海配一张可躺的床。

normal.en: The related compounds run seabed, seafloor, riverbed and lakebed.
normal.cn: 相关复合词包括 seabed、seafloor、riverbed 与 lakebed。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark law and industry: seabed lease, seabed mining, seabed survey.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律与工业用法：海床租约、海床采矿、海床勘测。

normal.en: The word is usually singular and takes the definite article: on the seabed.
normal.cn: 这个词通常用单数并带定冠词：on the seabed。

normal.en: British usage prefers seabed where American usage often says seafloor.
normal.cn: 英式用法偏好 seabed，而美式用法常说 seafloor。

abstract.en: Picture a bed of wet sand with no one lying on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张湿沙做的床，却没有人躺在上面。

abstract.en: Picture a buried boundary line drawn under the whole ocean.
abstract.cn: 想象整片海洋之下画着一条埋藏的界线。

abstract.en: Picture a field ploughed by anchors instead of ploughs.
abstract.cn: 想象一片被锚而非犁翻过的田地。

examples.en: The pipeline was buried beneath the seabed.
examples.cn: 管道被埋在海床之下。

examples.en: Trawling can damage the seabed over wide areas.
examples.cn: 拖网会大面积破坏海床。

examples.en: The survey found gas pockets just below the seabed.
examples.cn: 勘测发现海床正下方有气藏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sea（海）+ bed（床）」——海躺卧的那张床就是海床

root: 英语本族复合词：sea 来自古英语 sǣ「海」，bed 来自古英语 bedd「床、卧榻」；两词在日耳曼语之前的词根均为重构形式，复合词最早书证年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bed: the shallow bottom, the same bottom as owned land, its sediment skin, its use as a foundation, its living cover, its minerals, its relief, and its role as the line between water and soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一张床展开：浅海底、作为被拥有的土地、其沉积表皮、其作为地基的用途、其上的生物覆盖、其矿产、其起伏，以及其作为水与土界线的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet bed of sand and rock lying under a sheet of shallow water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层浅水之下湿沙与岩石构成的床面。

branches.en: TOUCHABLE BOTTOM: the shallow floor and its sediment surface.
branches.cn: 可触的底部：浅海底与其沉积表层。

branches.en: A DRAWN LINE: the bottom as owned land and as the boundary with subsoil.
branches.cn: 一条画出的线：海底作为被拥有的土地，也作为与底土的分界。

branches.en: FOUNDATION: cables and pipelines rest on the bed.
branches.cn: 地基：电缆与管道依托于这张床。

branches.en: LIVING COVER: oysters and worms turn the bed into habitat.
branches.cn: 生命覆盖：牡蛎与蠕虫把床面变成栖息地。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND RELIEF: the bed is both a mine and a landscape.
branches.cn: 资源与起伏：这张床既是矿场，也是地形。

intro.en: Seabed is a transparent Germanic compound of two common nouns, so its parts and its close compounds can be read without Latin help.
intro.cn: seabed 是两个常用名词构成的透明日耳曼语复合词，其组成部分与近邻复合词无需拉丁语知识即可读出。

latinIntro.en: Both sea and bed are Germanic, so the word has no Latin entries; Latin supplies the technical neighbours benthic and littoral instead.
latinIntro.cn: sea 与 bed 都属日耳曼语，因此这个词没有拉丁条目；拉丁语改为提供 benthic、littoral 这类技术近邻。

items.meaning: a resting place; a bottom layer
items.example: The bed of the stream was gravel.
The chart marks the sea bed in grey.

items.meaning: extraction of minerals from the sea bottom
a legal right to use a area of sea bottom
items.example: The firm won a seabed lease.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司获得了海床租约。

items.meaning: a systematic mapping of the bottom
items.example: The seabed survey took two months.
The sea-bed profile showed a channel.
items.exampleCN: 海床剖面显示出一条水道。

definition_en: a sea animal with flippers, a stamped mark, a closed fastening, or to close something tightly
core_image: 一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳，胡须上还挂着水珠
scene: 一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳。A seal lay on the ice in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 seal 是「海豹」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一只海豹趴在浮冰上晒太阳。

senses.title: A sea animal
senses.definition: a sea animal with flippers that rests on land or ice
senses.definitionCN: 有鳍状肢、在陆地或冰上休息的海洋动物
senses.example: A seal swam beside the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 一只海豹在船边游动。
senses.why: One word comes from an old name for this animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的一个来源就是这种动物的古称。

senses.title: A stamped mark
senses.definition: a device or mark pressed onto a document to prove it is genuine
senses.definitionCN: 盖在文件上以证明其真实的器具或印记
senses.example: The letter bore the king's seal.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信上有国王的印章。
senses.why: A pressed mark closes and certifies a document.
senses.whyCN: 压印的标记封闭并证明文件。

senses.title: A closed fastening
senses.definition: something that closes an opening tightly
senses.definitionCN: 把开口紧密封闭的东西
senses.example: The seal on the jar was broken.
senses.exampleCN: 罐子上的封口被打开了。
senses.why: The certified mark becomes a physical closure.
senses.whyCN: 认证标记变成物理封口。

senses.title: To close tightly
senses.definition: to close something so that air or liquid cannot pass
senses.definitionCN: 封闭某物使空气或液体无法通过
senses.example: She sealed the envelope with wax.
senses.exampleCN: 她用蜡把信封封好。
senses.why: The noun of closure becomes the action of closing.
senses.whyCN: 封闭物的名词义转为封闭动作。

intro.en: Seal is two words in one: Old English seolh, the animal, and Latin sigillum, a small stamp.
intro.cn: seal 是两个词合流：古英语 seolh（海豹）与拉丁语 sigillum（小图章）。

items.en: Seolh named the sea animal.
items.cn: seolh 指海豹这种海洋动物。

items.en: Sigillum meant a small picture or stamp.
items.cn: sigillum 意为小图像或印章。

items.en: Seel meant a stamp used on documents.
items.cn: seel 指用于文件的印章。

items.en: Seal named both the animal and the stamp.
items.cn: seal 同时指海豹与印章。

items.en: Seal also meant to close a document formally.
items.cn: seal 也开始表示正式封住文件。

items.en: Seal means to close tightly or to block an area.
items.cn: 现代英语中 seal 意为密封或封锁区域。

note.en: Seal is compared with similar short words and with words for stamps and closures.
note.cn: 把 seal 与形近短词以及表示印章和封闭的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small mark or device pressed on paper
a small seal, often in a ring

normalIntro.en: Seal is an animal and also a stamp that closes a document.
normalIntro.cn: seal 既是海豹，也是封住文件的印章。

normal.en: A seal lives in cold seas.
normal.cn: 海豹生活在寒冷海域。

normal.en: A wax seal closes a letter.
normal.cn: 蜡封印封住信件。

normal.en: Seal the envelope before posting.
normal.cn: 寄出前把信封封好。

normal.en: Police sealed off the street.
normal.cn: 警察封锁了街道。

normal.en: Seal and sea look alike.
normal.cn: seal 与 sea 形近。

abstract.en: Two unrelated words became one spelling.
abstract.cn: 两个无关的词变成了同一个拼写。

abstract.en: A stamp that proves a document also closes it.
abstract.cn: 证明文件的印章同时也封闭文件。

abstract.en: Closing and certifying share one gesture.
abstract.cn: 封闭与认证共享同一个动作。

examples.en: The envelope was sealed with wax.
examples.cn: 信封用蜡封好了。

examples.en: Police sealed off the street.
examples.cn: 警察封锁了街道。

examples.en: A seal swam beside the boat.
examples.cn: 一只海豹在船边游动。

dict_mnemonic.text: seal 有两个来源：古英语 seolh 指海豹，拉丁语 sigillum 指印章；「密封」义从盖印章封住文件发展而来。

root: 双源词：海豹义来自古英语 seolh；印章与密封义来自拉丁语 sigillum（小图章）。

sensesIntro.en: Seal means a sea animal, a stamped mark, a closure, or to close something tightly.
sensesIntro.cn: seal 意为海豹、印章、封口，或密封。

core.en: A mark or closure that makes something secure.
core.cn: 使某物安全可靠的印记或封闭。

branches.en: The animal of cold seas.
branches.cn: 寒冷海域的动物。

branches.en: A mark that proves a document.
branches.cn: 证明文件的印记。

branches.en: A physical closure on a container.
branches.cn: 容器上的物理封口。

branches.en: The action of closing tightly.
branches.cn: 紧密封闭的动作。

branches.en: Stamping and sealing both finish a document.
branches.cn: 盖章与密封都完成文件处理。

intro.en: Seal forms words for closing materials and actions.
intro.cn: seal 构成表示密封材料与动作的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin sigillum is the source of the stamp sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sigillum 是印章义的来源。

items.meaning: an animal, a stamp, or to close

items.example: Sealing the jar keeps food fresh.
items.exampleCN: 密封罐子能让食物保鲜。

items.meaning: a substance or person that seals

items.exampleCN: 法院公开了密封的记录。

items.example: He wore a silver seal ring.
items.exampleCN: 他戴着一枚银印章戒指。

definition_zh: 海藻；海草（生长在海里的大型藻类，也指采作食物或原料的海藻）
definition_en: large algae that grow in the sea, especially when gathered as food or raw material
core_image: 退潮后的礁石上挂着一片片湿滑的褐绿色长带，随残余的水流来回摆动
scene: 退潮后，渔妇蹲在湿滑的礁石上，用镰刀割下一长条褐绿色的海藻，抖了抖水放进竹篮。 At low tide she cut a long strand of seaweed from the wet rock and shook it into her basket.
sceneCN: 这里 seaweed 指「长在海里的大型藻类，可采集的海藻」（第 2 个义项：作为采集物或食材的海藻）；句意为退潮时她从湿滑的礁石上割下一长条海藻，抖掉水放进篮子。

pos.zh: 海藻；海草（大型海生藻类）
可食用的海藻；海藻制品

derivatives.zh: 带海藻味的；长满海藻的
海藻床（成片生长的海藻区）

senses.title: Marine algae growing in the sea
senses.definition: large algae that grow attached to rocks or the seabed in salt water
senses.definitionCN: 附着在礁石或海底生长的大型海生藻类
senses.example: Seaweed covered the rocks below the tide line.
senses.exampleCN: 潮线以下的礁石上覆满了海藻。
senses.why: The compound simply says 'a weed of the sea': sea names the place, weed names a plant-like growth, and the pair covers whatever grows there in sheets.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词字面就是「海里的草」：sea 标地点，weed 标像植物的生长物，合起来泛指成片长在那里的东西。

senses.title: Seaweed gathered as food
senses.definition: seaweed harvested and prepared for eating, fresh or dried
senses.definitionCN: 采收后新鲜或干燥食用的大型海藻
senses.example: She cut a long strand of seaweed from the wet rock.
senses.exampleCN: 她从湿滑的礁石上割下一长条海藻。
senses.why: Once people gather it deliberately, the word shifts from the plant in the sea to the crop in the basket.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人们有意采集，这个词就从「海里的植物」转为「篮子里的收成」。

senses.title: Raw material for industry
senses.definition: seaweed processed to extract gums, minerals or chemicals
senses.definitionCN: 经加工以提取胶质、矿物质或化学品的海藻
senses.example: Brown seaweed is processed for alginate used in food and medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 褐藻被加工成用于食品与医药的褐藻胶。
senses.why: The same harvest feeds factories, so the word also names a bulk material rather than a plant.
senses.whyCN: 同样的收成也供给工厂，因此这个词也指大宗原料，而不只是植物。

senses.title: Fertiliser spread on fields
senses.definition: seaweed used as mulch or soil improver on farmland
senses.definitionCN: 用作覆盖物或土壤改良剂的海藻
senses.example: Crofters spread seaweed on the potato beds each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 佃农每年春天把海藻铺在土豆地里。
senses.why: Coastal farming long used what the tide delivered, so seaweed became a word for free fertiliser.
senses.whyCN: 沿海农业长期利用潮水送来的东西，于是 seaweed 也成了「免费的肥料」。

senses.title: Weed cast up on the shore
senses.titleCN: 被浪冲上岸的腐烂海藻
senses.definition: seaweed washed ashore and left to rot along the high-water line
senses.definitionCN: 被冲上岸、在高潮线一带腐烂的海藻
senses.example: Flies rose from the seaweed at the high-water mark.
senses.exampleCN: 高潮线处的海藻上飞起一群苍蝇。
senses.why: Here the plant is dead and stranded; the word follows the material wherever the tide leaves it.
senses.whyCN: 此时植物已死并被搁浅，这个词跟着物质走，潮水把它留在哪里就指哪里。

senses.title: Underwater forest and habitat
senses.titleCN: 海藻林与其中的栖息地
senses.definition: a dense stand of large seaweed that shelters fish and invertebrates
senses.definitionCN: 为鱼类与无脊椎动物提供遮蔽的密集大型海藻群落
senses.example: Kelp, the tallest seaweed, forms forests along cold coasts.
senses.exampleCN: 海带是最高的海藻，在寒冷海岸形成森林。
senses.why: Ecology treats the mass as habitat, so seaweed names a place as well as a plant.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这一大片视为栖息地，因此 seaweed 既指植物也指地点。

senses.title: A sheet used to wrap food
senses.definition: a thin dried sheet of seaweed used to wrap rice or fillings
senses.definitionCN: 用来包米饭或馅料的干燥海藻薄片
senses.example: She wrapped the rice in a sheet of seaweed.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一片海藻把米饭卷起来。
senses.why: Cuisine turns the plant into a countable sheet, and the word follows the product's new shape.
senses.whyCN: 烹饪把植物变成可数的薄片，词义随之跟到成品的新形态上。

senses.title: A tangled mass, figuratively
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：纠缠成团的一大堆
senses.definition: a dense, disordered tangle that resembles seaweed in a harbour
senses.definitionCN: 像港里海藻那样密集而杂乱的一团东西
senses.example: A seaweed of old rope and nets clogged the repair shed.
senses.exampleCN: 一堆旧绳索和渔网像海藻一样缠塞了修理棚。
senses.why: The figurative use keeps only the shape of the mass: something long, wet and hopelessly entangled.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义只保留「一团」的形态：长长的、湿的、缠得解不开。

intro.en: Seaweed is a native English compound of sea and weed, not a borrowing; its two halves are both Old English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: seaweed 是英语本族复合词，由 sea 与 weed 组成，并非外来借词；两半都来自古英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sǣ meant 'sea, lake, sheet of water' and survives in sea, as well as in compounds such as sea-bird and sea-wall.
items.cn: sǣ 意为「海、湖、大片水域」，留存为 sea，也见于 sea-bird、sea-wall 等复合词。

items.en: Wēod meant 'herb, grass, plant', with no hint of nuisance; the modern sense 'unwanted plant' developed later.
items.cn: wēod 意为「草、植物」，本无「有害」之意；现代「杂草」义是后来才发展出来的。

items.en: The compound sea + weed is recorded in the sixteenth century for plants of the sea; the exact first citation is not settled, so the date is approximate.
items.cn: sea + weed 的复合形式在 16 世纪有记录，指海中的植物；确切的最早书证尚无定论，因此年代为约数。

items.en: Modern botany limits seaweed to large algae; seagrasses are flowering plants and are therefore not seaweeds, a distinction everyday use often ignores.
items.cn: 现代植物学把 seaweed 限制为大型藻类；海草是开花植物，因此不算海藻，但日常用法常忽略这一区别。

items.en: From the nineteenth century seaweed was harvested for iodine and potash, and later for alginates, food and feed.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，海藻被采收用于制碘与钾碱，后来又用于褐藻胶、食品与饲料。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-English origin of weed is unsettled, and the earliest date of the compound is approximate rather than a fixed citation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：weed 在英语之前的来源没有定论，复合词的最早年代也只是约数，而非确切书证。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that are often mistaken for the same thing; group two holds words for edible sea plants that overlap without being synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误认为同一种东西的形近词；第二组是可食海生植物的近义词，彼此重叠但并非同义。

entries.definition: Built from sea + -ward 'in the direction of', it means toward the sea and has nothing to do with weed.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sea + -ward「朝……方向」构成，意为朝海的方向，与 weed 无关。

entries.definition: A marine flowering plant with roots and flowers, not an alga; the name looks parallel but the biology is different.
entries.definitionCN: 有根有花的海洋开花植物，不是藻类；名称结构相似，但生物类别不同。

entries.definition: Wrack is seaweed, especially when washed ashore; sea wrack overlaps with seaweed but usually names the stranded mass.
entries.definitionCN: wrack 指海藻，尤指冲上岸的；sea wrack 与 seaweed 重叠，但通常指搁浅的那一堆。

entries.definition: Seaweed is the large, visible member of the algae; the group also contains single-celled forms never called seaweed.
entries.definitionCN: 海藻是藻类中大型、可见的成员；藻类还包括从不被称为 seaweed 的单细胞种类。

entries.definition: A kind of very large brown seaweed forming underwater forests; it is a seaweed, but not every seaweed is kelp.
entries.definitionCN: 一种形成海底森林的超大型褐藻；kelp 属于海藻，但并非所有海藻都是 kelp。

entries.definition: Seaweed of the shore, especially brown kinds cast up by the tide; the word stresses the stranded state.
entries.definitionCN: 岸边的海藻，尤指被潮水冲上岸的褐藻；这个词强调被搁浅的状态。

entries.definition: A Japanese term for dried laver sheets; it names one prepared food, while seaweed is the general material.
entries.definitionCN: 日语词，指干燥的紫菜片；它指一种成品食物，而 seaweed 是泛称的原料。

entries.definition: A red seaweed eaten dried in northern Europe; again a member of the seaweed family rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 北欧常晒干食用的一种红藻；同样是海藻家族的一员，而非同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sea + weed: a plant-like growth of the sea, read literally.
normal.cn: sea + weed：字面就是「海里的草状生长物」。

normal.en: Seaweed is uncountable as a mass but countable as kinds: seaweed on the rocks, seaweeds of the tropics.
normal.cn: 作物质时不可数，作种类时可数：礁石上的 seaweed，热带的多种 seaweeds。

normal.en: Seagrass is not seaweed: it flowers, has roots, and belongs with land plants.
normal.cn: seagrass 不是 seaweed：它有花有根，属于陆生植物的近亲。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: seaweed extract, seaweed farming, seaweed soup, seaweed bed.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：海藻提取物、海藻养殖、海藻汤、海藻床。

normal.en: The industrial product alginate comes from brown seaweed, which links the food word to chemistry.
normal.cn: 工业产品 alginate 来自褐藻，这把食物词与化学连了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a green ribbon that keeps waving even after the wave has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿色的带子，浪走了它还在摆。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of the sea carried home on a woman's back.
abstract.cn: 想象一篮「海」被背回家。

abstract.en: Picture a tangled heap of nets that looks like it grew on the quay.
abstract.cn: 想象码头上一堆缠结的渔网，像是从岸上长出来的海藻。

examples.en: Seaweed on the rocks keeps the shore cool and wet at low tide.
examples.cn: 礁石上的海藻在退潮时为岸边保冷保湿。

examples.en: The farm grows seaweed for food and for alginate.
examples.cn: 这个养殖场养殖海藻，用于食用和提取褐藻胶。

examples.en: A thick layer of seaweed marked where the storm tide had reached.
examples.cn: 厚厚一层海藻标出了风暴潮抵达的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: sea（海）+ weed（草）——海里的草就是海藻；看到礁石上的绿带子就想这个词

root: 英语本族复合词：sea（古英语 sǣ「海」）+ weed（古英语 wēod「草、植物」）；weed 的更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one material through its uses: the plant in the sea, the crop in the basket, the raw material in the factory, the mulch on the field, the wrack on the strand, the forest under water, the sheet on the plate, and finally the tangle in the harbour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一种材料穿过各种用途：海里的植物、篮里的收成、厂里的原料、田里的肥料、滩上的搁浅物、水下的森林、盘上的薄片，最后是港口的缠结。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wet green ribbons hanging from rocks, water still dripping from them.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿漉漉的绿带子挂在礁石上，水还在往下滴。

branches.en: WHERE IT LIES: alive on the rock or dead on the strand, the word stays with the material.
branches.cn: 它在哪儿：活着长在石上，或死了搁在滩上，词都跟着这份材料走。

branches.en: FOOD: the harvest is eaten fresh, dried, or pressed into sheets.
branches.cn: 食物：收成可鲜食、晒干，或压成薄片。

branches.en: WORKING MATERIAL: factories extract gums, farms dig it into the soil.
branches.cn: 可用之材：工厂提炼胶质，农田把它翻进土里。

branches.en: HABITAT: a dense stand becomes a forest that shelters other life.
branches.cn: 栖息地：密集的一片成了庇护其他生命的森林。

branches.en: SHAPE ALONE: the figurative sense keeps only the long, wet, tangled look.
branches.cn: 只剩形态：比喻义只保留长、湿、缠结的样子。

intro.en: Seaweed is a compound, so its two free morphemes can be read separately and then recombined in other words.
intro.cn: seaweed 是复合词，两个自由语素可以分开读，再组合进别的词。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: sea and weed are native English words. The Latin-based relatives are algae, algal and alginate, borrowed separately.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：sea 与 weed 是英语本族词。以拉丁为源的亲属词 algae、algal、alginate 是另行借入的。

items.example: The compound names the place of growth.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前半标出生长地点。

items.example: The second half names the plant-like growth.
items.exampleCN: 后半标出像植物的生长物。

items.example: The bay holds dozens of seaweeds.
items.exampleCN: 这个海湾有数十种海藻。

items.meaningCN: 带海藻味的；覆满海藻的
items.example: The cove was seaweedy at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 退潮时这个小湾到处是海藻。

items.meaning: a patch where seaweed grows thickly
items.example: Fish shelter in the seaweed bed.

items.exampleCN: 这款乳液含海藻提取物。

items.example: Seaweed farming spread along the cold coast.
items.exampleCN: 海藻养殖在寒冷海岸推广开来。

definition_zh: 次要的；中学的；第二位的；继发的
definition_en: less important than something else, relating to secondary school, coming second in order, or resulting from something else
core_image: 主干道旁的分岔小路，路口立着一块不起眼的小牌子
scene: 主路堵得水泄不通，他拐进一条次要的小路。He took a secondary road to avoid the traffic.
sceneCN: 这里 secondary 是「次要的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他走一条次要道路以避开拥堵。

senses.title: Less important
senses.definition: less important than the main thing
senses.definitionCN: 不如主要事物重要
senses.example: Safety is never a secondary concern.
senses.exampleCN: 安全从来都不是次要问题。
senses.why: This is the broad everyday sense of lower priority.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示优先级较低的宽泛日常义。

senses.title: Of secondary school
senses.definition: relating to education for older children
senses.definitionCN: 与较大儿童的教育有关
senses.example: She teaches at a secondary school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所中学教书。
senses.why: The school level comes after primary education.
senses.whyCN: 中学阶段在小学教育之后。

senses.title: Coming second
senses.definition: second in order, rank, or level
senses.definitionCN: 在顺序、等级或层次上居第二
senses.example: The report relied on secondary sources.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告依赖二手资料。
senses.why: A second-hand source is one step from the original.
senses.whyCN: 二手资料与原初来源隔了一步。

senses.title: Resulting from something
senses.definition: caused by or developing from an earlier condition
senses.definitionCN: 由先前状况引起或由此发展而来
senses.example: The doctor treated a secondary infection.
senses.exampleCN: 医生治疗了继发感染。
senses.why: Medical use names a condition that follows another.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法指紧随另一状况出现的病症。

intro.en: Secondary comes from Latin secundarius, from secundus, following or second.
intro.cn: secondary 源自拉丁语 secundarius，出自 secundus（跟随的、第二的）。

items.en: Secundus meant following or second.
items.cn: secundus 意为跟随的或第二的。

items.en: Secundarius meant of the second rank.
items.cn: secundarius 意为第二等级的。

items.en: Secondary entered English as a word for second rank.
items.cn: secondary 以「第二等级」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word described subordinate things and school levels.
items.cn: 该词用来形容从属事物与学校阶段。

items.en: Medicine added the sense of a following condition.
items.cn: 医学又增加了「继发状况」的义项。

note.en: Secondary is compared with similar-looking words and with words for lesser importance.
note.cn: 把 secondary 与形近词以及表示较次要的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Secondary means second in importance, level, or origin.
normalIntro.cn: secondary 意为在重要性、层级或来源上居第二。

normal.en: Secondary school follows primary school.
normal.cn: secondary school 是小学之后的中学。

normal.en: A secondary source is not the original.
normal.cn: secondary source 不是原始资料。

normal.en: Secondary means less important, not useless.
normal.cn: secondary 表示较次要，而非毫无用处。

normal.en: A secondary infection follows the first one.
normal.cn: secondary infection 是继发于初次感染的。

normal.en: Secondary shares its root with second.
normal.cn: secondary 与 second 同根。

abstract.en: Calling something secondary is a way of ranking the world.
abstract.cn: 称某事为次要，是在给世界排位。

abstract.en: What is secondary can still decide the outcome.
abstract.cn: 次要因素有时仍能决定结果。

abstract.en: Every first needs a second to follow it.
abstract.cn: 每一个第一都需要一个跟随的第二。

examples.en: Safety is never a secondary concern.
examples.cn: 安全从来都不是次要问题。

examples.en: She teaches at a secondary school.
examples.cn: 她在一所中学教书。

examples.en: The report relied on secondary sources.
examples.cn: 这份报告依赖二手资料。

dict_mnemonic.text: secondary 由 second（第二）加形容词后缀 -ary 构成，表示「排在第二位的、次要的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 secundarius（第二等级的），出自 secundus（第二），核心义「居其次的」。

sensesIntro.en: Secondary means less important, relating to secondary school, second in rank, or following another condition.
sensesIntro.cn: secondary 意为次要的、中学的、第二位的，或继发的。

core.en: Something that follows and ranks below a first.
core.cn: 跟随在第一之后、等级较低的事物。

branches.en: A matter of lower priority.
branches.cn: 优先级较低的事项。

branches.en: The school level after primary.
branches.cn: 小学之后的学校阶段。

branches.en: A rank or source one step from the first.
branches.cn: 距第一等一步之遥的等级或来源。

branches.en: A condition that follows another.
branches.cn: 紧随另一状况出现的病症。

branches.en: Lower importance and second rank often mean the same.
branches.cn: 较低重要性与第二等级常常是同一回事。

intro.en: Secondary builds on second, with words for order and priority.
intro.cn: secondary 以 second 为基础，构成表示顺序与优先级的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin secundus and secundarius are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secundus 与 secundarius 是历史词根。

items.example: He finished second in the race.
items.exampleCN: 他在比赛中获得第二名。

items.meaning: second helpings or units of time
items.example: The clock ticked away the seconds.

items.exampleCN: 其次，我们需要更多时间。

items.example: The fund is used primarily, not secondarily.
items.exampleCN: 这笔资金用于主要用途，而非次要用途。

items.example: The secondariness of the issue was clear.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题的次要性很清楚。

items.example: They settled for a second-best option.
The parcel went by second-class mail.

definition_zh: 秘密；秘诀；秘密的；保密的
definition_en: something kept hidden from others, a method that works very well, or kept from public knowledge
core_image: 抽屉最里层压着一封没有署名的信，封口已经被摩挲得发白
scene: 她压低声音，把这件事只告诉了最好的朋友。She kept the secret from everyone else.
sceneCN: 这里 secret 是「秘密」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她对其他所有人都保守这个秘密。

senses.title: Something hidden
senses.definition: a fact or piece of information kept from others
senses.definitionCN: 对他人隐瞒的事实或信息
senses.example: She told me a secret.
senses.exampleCN: 她告诉了我一个秘密。
senses.why: This is the central everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的日常义。

senses.title: A working method
senses.definition: a method or trick that produces a good result
senses.definitionCN: 能带来好结果的方法或窍门
senses.example: The recipe is a family secret.
senses.exampleCN: 这个配方是家族秘诀。

intro.en: Secret comes from Latin secretus, set apart or hidden, from secernere, to separate.
intro.cn: secret 源自拉丁语 secretus（分开的、隐藏的），出自 secernere（分离）。

items.en: Secernere meant to separate or set apart.
items.cn: secernere 意为分开或隔离。

items.en: Secretus meant hidden or withdrawn.
items.cn: secretus 意为隐藏的或退避的。

items.en: Secret named something kept from view.
items.cn: secret 表示被藏起来的事物。

items.en: Secret entered English as both noun and adjective.
items.cn: secret 作为名词和形容词进入英语。

items.en: The word also names a special working method.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也指特别的方法。

note.en: Secret is compared with similar-looking words and with words for hidden things.
note.cn: 把 secret 与形近词以及表示隐藏之物的词作比较。

entries.definition: the state of being kept hidden

normalIntro.en: A secret is hidden information, a hidden method, or the quality of being hidden.
normalIntro.cn: secret 是被隐藏的信息、隐藏的方法，或被隐藏的状态。

normal.en: Keep a secret means not telling others.
normal.cn: keep a secret 意为不告诉别人。

normal.en: In secret means quietly and privately.
normal.cn: in secret 意为悄悄地、私下地。

normal.en: Top secret is the highest level of secrecy.
normal.cn: top secret 是最高保密级别。

normal.en: The secret of success is a hidden working method.
normal.cn: the secret of success 指隐藏的成功方法。

normal.en: Secret and secretary share the same Latin root.
normal.cn: secret 与 secretary 共享拉丁词根。

abstract.en: A secret is something set apart from public view.
abstract.cn: 秘密是被从公众视野中分隔出来的事物。

abstract.en: Keeping a secret is a kind of power and a kind of burden.
abstract.cn: 保守秘密既是一种权力，也是一种负担。

abstract.en: A method becomes a secret when it is not shared.
abstract.cn: 方法不被分享时就成了秘诀。

intro.en: Section comes from Latin sectio, a cutting, from secare, to cut.
intro.cn: section 源自拉丁语 sectio（切割），出自 secare（切）。

items.en: Secare meant to cut.
items.cn: secare 意为切。

items.en: Sectio meant a cutting or a piece cut off.
items.cn: sectio 意为切割或切下的部分。

items.en: Section entered English as a part cut from a whole.
items.cn: section 以「从整体切下的部分」进入英语。

items.en: Books and organizations began to use sections.
items.cn: 书籍与组织开始使用 section 划分。

items.en: The word also names a technical cross-section.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也指技术性的横截面。

note.en: Section is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parts.
note.cn: 把 section 与形近词以及表示部分的词作比较。

entries.definition: a part of an economy or a pie slice
a period of activity or meeting

normalIntro.en: A section is a part cut from a whole, whether a road, a shop, a book, or a pipe.
normalIntro.cn: section 是从整体切下的一部分，无论是道路、商店、书还是管道。

normal.en: Section and sector both come from a root meaning to cut.
normal.cn: section 与 sector 都出自表示「切」的词根。

normal.en: A newspaper has a sports section and a business section.
normal.cn: 报纸有体育版和商业版。

normal.en: Read the report section by section.
normal.cn: 要一部分一部分地读报告。

normal.en: A cross section shows the inside of an object.
normal.cn: 横截面展示物体内部。

normal.en: A subsection is a smaller section inside one.
normal.cn: subsection 是章节内更小的节。

abstract.en: To understand a whole, we cut it into sections.
abstract.cn: 为了理解整体，我们把它切成部分。

abstract.en: Every section belongs to something larger.
abstract.cn: 每个部分都属于某个更大的整体。

abstract.en: A cross section reveals what the surface hides.
abstract.cn: 横截面揭示表面所隐藏的东西。

examples.en: This section of the road is closed.
examples.cn: 这段路封闭了。

examples.en: She works in the sports section.
examples.cn: 她在体育部工作。

examples.en: Read the first section of the report.
examples.cn: 读报告的第一节。
